title: The Push to Revise American History at the Smithsonian

sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.zh: 我在凌晨4点半打电话给总统，他接了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 七十年的太空探索。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗星星的背后有什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费者产品指南。

sentences.zh: 今天我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60款超级圣代冰淇淋。

sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟里最好的球队。

And I love a one-pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》庆祝成立175周年，致力于帮您理解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 立即订阅，享受nytimes.com/subscribe上的特惠。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Rachel Abrams and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的雷切尔·艾布拉姆斯，这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: President Trump is now calling for an overhaul to the museums in the United States.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统现在呼吁对美国的博物馆进行彻底改革。

sentences.en: The president accusing the Smithsonian of making our country look horrible by focusing on topics like, quote, how bad slavery was.
sentences.zh: 总统指责史密森尼学会通过关注诸如“奴隶制有多糟糕”之类的话题，让我们的国家看起来很糟糕。

sentences.en: In the last few weeks, the Trump administration has turned its sights on the Smithsonian, the latest target in a campaign to remake cultural institutions in its image.
sentences.zh: 在过去的几周里，特朗普政府将目光投向了史密森尼学会，这是其按照自身形象重塑文化机构运动中的最新目标。

sentences.en: The White House will be reviewing material in some of the museums to make sure that they align with the president's view of history.
sentences.zh: 白宫将审查部分博物馆中的材料，以确保它们符合总统对历史的看法。

sentences.en: Officials are attempting to change exhibits at the center of the country's culture wars and reshape American history at one of the largest museum complexes in the world.
sentences.zh: 官员们正试图改变处于国家文化战争核心的展览，并在世界最大的博物馆群之一重塑美国历史。

sentences.en: We want the museums to treat our country fairly.
sentences.zh: 我们希望博物馆公正对待我们的国家。

sentences.en: We want the museums to talk about the history of our country in a fair manner, not in a woke manner or in a racist manner.
sentences.zh: 我们希望博物馆以公平的方式谈论我们国家的历史，而不是以“觉醒”或种族主义的方式。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Robin Pogobin on the fight over who gets to tell the American story and how.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事罗宾·波戈宾将探讨关于谁来讲述美国故事以及如何讲述的争夺战。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, September 3rd.
sentences.zh: 今天是9月3日，星期三。

sentences.en: Robin, since taking office, the Trump administration has been trying to exert control over some of America's most important cultural institutions.
sentences.zh: 罗宾，自上任以来，特朗普政府一直试图对美国一些最重要的文化机构施加控制。

sentences.en: And it really feels like we're seeing that effort crescendo at the Smithsonian, which you have been paying a lot of attention to.
sentences.zh: 而且感觉这种努力真的在史密森尼学会达到了高潮，这也是你一直高度关注的。

sentences.en: You are a reporter who has for a very long time covered arts and culture in the United States.
sentences.zh: 你是一位长期报道美国艺术与文化的记者。

sentences.en: Can you tell us what has been happening?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我们发生了什么吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, so it's been a remarkable few months that amounts to essentially a wholesale attack on the arts.
sentences.zh: 是的，过去几个月非同寻常，基本上相当于对艺术界发起了全面攻击。

sentences.en: I think what's been happening, you can see most clearly in a recent post from President Trump himself, where he described museums as the last remaining segment of woke.
sentences.zh: 我认为正在发生的事情，你可以从特朗普总统本人最近的一篇帖子中最清楚地看到，他将博物馆描述为“觉醒”的最后残余。

sentences.en: And he called the Smithsonian in particular out of control.
sentences.zh: 他特别称史密森尼学会已经失控。

sentences.en: And to go after an institution as big and prestigious and as critical to American culture as the Smithsonian is just a really dramatic escalation.
sentences.zh: 而去针对一个像史密森尼学会这样规模庞大、声誉卓著且对美国文化至关重要的机构，绝对是一个非常巨大的升级。

sentences.en: Why does the attack on the Smithsonian feel like such an escalation?
sentences.zh: 为什么对史密森尼学会的攻击感觉像是如此大的升级？

sentences.en: Well, the Smithsonian has both historic and symbolic power.
sentences.zh: 嗯，史密森尼学会既拥有历史权力，也拥有象征权力。

sentences.en: It is comprised of 21 museums, as well as libraries, research centers, and the National Zoo.
sentences.zh: 它由21家博物馆以及图书馆、研究中心和国家动物园组成。

sentences.en: A lot of those museums are on the National Mall.
sentences.zh: 其中许多博物馆都位于国家广场上。

sentences.en: It is very much a tourist destination.
sentences.zh: 它完全是一个旅游目的地。

sentences.en: It's free.
sentences.zh: 它是免费的。

sentences.en: And also it is considered America's Attic, a repository of U.S.
sentences.zh: 而且它也被认为是美国的阁楼，是美国文化和历史的存储库。

sentences.en: culture and history.
sentences.zh: 这里有来自世界各地的艺术品和文物的珍贵部分，以及对我们来说非常熟悉和标志性的东西，

sentences.en: It has important pieces of art and artifacts from all over the world and things that are very familiar and iconic to us,
sentences.zh: 比如最初启发了美国国歌的星条旗，莱特兄弟的第一架飞机。

sentences.en: like the Star-Spangled Banner flag that originally inspired the National Anthem, the Wright Brothers' first airplane.
sentences.zh: 但它也有一些东西，比如民权静坐抗议活动中最初的快餐柜台，以及加州日军集中营的一些标牌。

sentences.en: But it also has things like the original lunch counter from the Civil Rights sit-ins and some of the signage from Japanese internment camps in California.
sentences.zh: 所以这真的是一个范围广泛的收藏。

sentences.en: So really a wide-ranging collection.
sentences.zh: 对，完全如此。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 而且史密森尼学会10亿美元年度预算中，超过一半来自政府，占到62%。

sentences.en: And the Smithsonian gets more than half of its $1 billion annual budget from the government, 62%.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，这是一个独立的机构。

sentences.en: But that said, this is an independent institution.
sentences.zh: 它历来也是这样运作的。

sentences.en: It has historically operated as such.
sentences.zh: 这意味着艺术决策是由博物馆馆长和策展人做出的，而不是由董事会决定，也不是由政府决定。

sentences.en: And that means that artistic decisions are made by museum directors and curators and not by the board and not by the government.
sentences.zh: 作为一个自主运营、做自己事情的机构，它一直极其成功。

sentences.en: And it has been extremely successful as an institution running itself and doing its own thing.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，不仅来自政府的这种干预，

sentences.en: And that is why this is such a big deal to have this kind of an intervention from not only the government,
sentences.zh: 而且来自总统本人对这些博物馆展品细节的兴趣，才显得如此重要。

sentences.en: but from the president himself taking an interest in the minutiae of what these museums show.
sentences.zh: 所有这些干预史密森尼学会独立性的努力以及这种对艺术界的普遍接管，这个故事到底是从哪里开始的？

sentences.en: All of these efforts to interfere in the independence of the Smithsonian and sort of this general takeover of the arts, where does that story start exactly?
sentences.zh: 事实上，我认为这个故事确实是从华盛顿的另一个文化地标——肯尼迪表演艺术中心开始的。

sentences.en: Actually, I think the story really starts with another cultural icon in Washington, the Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts.
sentences.zh: 它不是史密森尼学会的一部分，但它位于国家的首都。

sentences.en: It's not part of the Smithsonian, but it is in the nation's capital.
sentences.zh: 这也是特朗普总统重返白宫后首次将注意力集中在那里。

sentences.en: And it's where President Trump first focused his attention when he returned to office.
sentences.zh: 在2月份，他指责该中心的节目编排过于“觉醒”。

sentences.en: In February, he accused the center of programming that was too woke.
sentences.zh: 他抱怨变装皇后在那里表演。

sentences.en: He complained about drag queens performing there.
sentences.zh: 他在一条推文中称其为反美宣传。

sentences.en: He said in one tweet that it was anti-American propaganda.
sentences.zh: 他甚至采取行动清除了董事会中的拜登任命人员，让自己当选为主席，

sentences.en: And he went so far as to eliminate the Biden appointees on the board, to get himself elected as chairman,
sentences.zh: 并安插了一位他最忠实的盟友担任临时总裁。

sentences.en: and to install an interim president of one of his kind of most loyal associates.
sentences.zh: 同样令人震惊的是，肯尼迪中心主席大卫·鲁恩斯坦决定默默接受这一切。

sentences.en: And it was also striking that the chairman of the Kennedy Center, David Rubenstein, decided to just kind of go quietly.
sentences.zh: 对此并没有引起任何真正的愤怒或抗议。

sentences.en: There wasn't any real outrage or protest in reaction to this.
sentences.zh: 我认为这在一定程度上助长了特朗普政府索求更多东西的胃口。

sentences.en: And I think it kind of whet the appetite of the Trump administration for more.
sentences.zh: 他们看到了这套剧本的成功，因此转向了另一个典型的美国机构，即史密森尼学会。

sentences.en: They saw the success of this playbook and therefore turned to another kind of quintessentially American institution, which was the Smithsonian.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统做了什么？

sentences.en: And what did President Trump do?
sentences.zh: 所以在3月份，总统发布了一项行政令，基本上指责史密森尼学会试图推广一种分裂的、以种族为中心的意识形态，

sentences.en: So in March, the president issues an executive order that essentially accuses the Smithsonian of trying to promote a divisive, race-centered ideology,
sentences.zh: 描述了他所看到的破坏美国的修正主义运动，

sentences.en: describing what he sees as a revisionist movement that undermines the United States
sentences.zh: 其叙事方式以有害和压迫性的方式描绘了美国和西方价值观。

sentences.en: in terms of narratives that portray America and Western values in a way that's harmful and oppressive.
sentences.zh: 因此，他所做的是加大了推行其美国历史愿景的力度。

sentences.en: So instead, what he did was intensified his push to impose his vision of American history.
sentences.zh: 那是一种更加积极的愿景，要求史密森尼把自己变成灵感和美国伟大的象征，

sentences.en: And that is one that is more positive, that demands that the Smithsonian make itself into a symbol of inspiration
sentences.zh: 而不是专注于我们传统中比较消极的方面。

sentences.en: and American greatness, rather than focus on the more negative aspects of our heritage.
sentences.zh: 那么这具体是怎样的呢？

sentences.en: So what does that look like exactly?
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先是特朗普公开呼吁解雇国家肖像馆馆长金·萨耶特。

sentences.en: Well, it starts with Trump publicly calling for the firing of the National Portrait Gallery director, Kim Sayet.
sentences.zh: 国家肖像馆也许是史密森尼最重要的博物馆之一，因为它包含了被认为是每一位总统官方肖像的所有画作。

sentences.en: The National Portrait Gallery is perhaps one of the most important Smithsonian museums because it contains all of these what are considered official portraits of every president.
sentences.zh: 这些对公众有着巨大的吸引力。

sentences.en: And those are a huge draw for the public.
sentences.zh: 萨耶特毫不掩饰她对重新构想博物馆和做出有意义改变的兴趣。

sentences.en: And Sayet made no secret of her interest in reimagining the museum and making meaningful changes.
sentences.zh: 她在2022年告诉我们，几个世纪以来，博物馆里的肖像和半身像都是为了捕捉精英的形象而保留的，

sentences.en: She told us in 2022 that for centuries, portraits and busts in the museum were reserved for capturing images of the elite
sentences.zh: 这留下了一份扭曲的历史记录，在很大程度上仅限于“富有的人、苍白的人和男性”。

sentences.en: and that that had left a distorted historical record that was largely limited to, quote, the wealthy, the pale, and the male.
sentences.zh: 正是这句话被特朗普政府捕捉到了，他们称她为“一个高度党派化的人和DEI（多元、公平、包容）的坚定支持者”，

sentences.en: And it was actually that very phrase that the Trump administration picked up on and calling her, quote, a highly partisan person and a strong supporter of DEI,
sentences.zh: 这对于她的职位来说是完全不合适的。

sentences.en: which is totally inappropriate for her position.
sentences.zh: 那么肖像馆对这一切作何反应？

sentences.en: And so how does the Portrait Gallery respond to all of this?
sentences.zh: 嗯，最初史密森尼学会董事会所做的，因为那是管理史密森尼的治理机构，

sentences.en: Well, initially, what the Smithsonian Board of Regents did, because that is the kind of governing body that runs the Smithsonian,
sentences.zh: 是他们表示这不是总统的管辖范围。

sentences.en: was they said that this is not the purview of the president.
sentences.zh: 这是我们的。

sentences.en: It's ours.
sentences.zh: 但我们会将您的关切纳入考量并进行我们自己的审查。

sentences.en: But we will take your concerns into consideration and do our own review.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，非常感谢您的意见，但您不能就这样解雇我们某家博物馆的负责人。

sentences.en: In other words, thank you so much for your input, but you can't just fire the head of one of our museuMs.
sentences.zh: 这不是您的工作。

sentences.en: That's not your job.
sentences.zh: 这是我们的工作。

sentences.en: That's our job.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 但我们会考虑您的投诉。

sentences.en: But we will consider your complaints.
sentences.zh: 我们将与其他所有博物馆一起评估肖像馆是否存在偏见，并真诚地努力回应您的关切。

sentences.en: We will evaluate the Portrait Gallery for Bias along with all of our other museums and kind of make a good faith effort to respond to your concerns.
sentences.zh: 显然，这证明对特朗普政府来说是不够的。

sentences.en: That obviously did not prove sufficient for the Trump administration.
sentences.zh: 而且实际上，施加的压力也确实变得太大了。

sentences.en: And also, actually, the pressure that was brought to bear actually became too much.
sentences.zh: 在这一切发生后的两周内，她自愿离职了。

sentences.en: And she left of her own accord within two weeks of all of this.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，尽管史密森尼可能试图表现得像是在妥协，但政府最终还是得到了它想要的。

sentences.en: So basically, even though the Smithsonian maybe tried to seem like it was compromising, the administration does eventually get what it wanted.
sentences.zh: 比如，她在被解雇的威胁下辞职了。

sentences.en: Like, she resigns under threat of firing.
sentences.zh: 这也说明了史密森尼理事会在试图走这条钢丝——既想满足特朗普政府又不惹恼它，同时还要坚持自身的使命和原则——方面所做出的努力。

sentences.en: It also spoke to an effort on the part of the Smithsonian Governing Board to walk this line between trying to satisfy the Trump administration and not antagonize it
sentences.zh: 而处于这一核心并领导这一努力的人是其秘书朗尼·邦奇。

sentences.en: while adhere to its own kind of mission and principles.
sentences.zh: 他是谁？

sentences.en: And the person at the heart of that and leading that effort is its secretary, Lonnie Bunch.
sentences.zh: 他的背景是什么？

sentences.en: And who is he?
sentences.zh: 朗尼·邦奇是史密森尼学会的第一位黑人秘书。

sentences.en: What is his background?
sentences.zh: 他在这个职位上已经六年了，他作为美国国家非裔美国人历史与文化博物馆的创办馆长而闻名，

sentences.en: Lonnie Bunch is the first Black secretary to serve at the Smithsonian.
sentences.zh: 该博物馆于2016年盛大开馆，去年迎来了160万游客。

sentences.en: He's been in the job for six years, and he kind of made a name for himself as the founding director of the National Museum of African-American History and Culture,
sentences.zh: 邦奇成功做到的是确保这不是一个充满争议的博物馆，就像大多数史密森尼博物馆随着时间推移所呈现的那样。

sentences.en: which opened to great fanfare in 2016 and last year had 1.6 million visitors.
sentences.zh: 它们通常相当温和，在历史层面上并不具有挑衅性。

sentences.en: And what Bunch succeeded in doing is making sure that this was not a controversial museum, as most Smithsonian museums have not been over time.
sentences.zh: 尽管这是一个关于一些非常困难话题的博物馆，

sentences.en: They are generally fairly benign and not provocative historically.
sentences.zh: 邦奇还是成功为其筹集了资金，并争取到了民主党和共和党对它的支持。

sentences.en: And even though this was a museum that was about some very difficult topics,
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Bunch managed to raise money for it and kind of enlist both Democrats and Republicans in supporting it.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他在所有这些博物馆里的工作就是让它们尽可能地对广大公众开放和具有吸引力。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Basically, his job at all of these museums is to make them as open and inviting to the general public as possible.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 这些应该是吸引广大公众的博物馆，理想情况下不疏远任何特定的群体。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 这是一个让所有美国人都感到宾至如归的地方。

sentences.en: These should be museums that appeal to a broad public and ideally don't alienate any particular groups.
sentences.zh: 但走这种温和的中道路线变得越来越困难。

sentences.en: And it's a place where all Americans feel comfortable coming.
sentences.zh: 这种矛盾在今年夏天真正升级了，当时艺术家艾米·谢拉德本应在国家肖像馆举办一场大型展览。

sentences.en: But walking that kind of moderate centrist line has become more and more difficult.
sentences.zh: 所以艾米·谢拉德是一位杰出的画家。

sentences.en: And it really escalated over the summer where the artist Amy Sherald was supposed to have a major exhibition at the National Portrait Gallery.
sentences.zh: 她广受赞誉，也是最著名的画家之一。

sentences.en: So Amy Sherald is a prominent painter.
sentences.zh: 她凭借这幅米歇尔·奥巴马的官方肖像真正崭露头角。

sentences.en: She's been widely celebrated and she's the most famous.
sentences.zh: 这位艺术家有一个大型回顾展刚刚在纽约展出，原本应该在今年秋天巡展到华盛顿。

sentences.en: She really broke out with this official portrait of Michelle Obama.
sentences.zh: 但该展览中的一幅画作显然开始让史密森尼董事会的一些成员感到紧张。

sentences.en: And the artist has a big retrospective that was just in New York and was supposed to travel on next to Washington this fall.
sentences.zh: 为什么会这样？

sentences.en: But there was one painting in that exhibition that apparently started to make some members of the Smithsonian board nervous.
sentences.zh: 跟我说说这幅画吧。

sentences.en: Why is that?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这幅画描绘了一个跨性别的自由女神像。

sentences.en: Tell me about the painting.
sentences.zh: 它被称为《蜕变的自由》。

sentences.en: Well, the painting depicts a transgender Statue of Liberty.
sentences.zh: 它真实地展现了一个自豪的黑人跨性别女性高举火炬。

sentences.en: It's called Transforming Liberty.
sentences.zh: 这体现了谢拉德作品的标志，她的作品通常具有政治内涵，并引发了关于性别认同和种族的问题。

sentences.en: It really shows a proud black trans woman holding the torch.
sentences.zh: 我认为史密森尼董事会开始担心，这正是那种会惹恼特朗普政府的敏感议题。

sentences.en: And it's emblematic of Sherald's work, which often has political undertones and raises issues of gender identity and race.
sentences.zh: 而他们并不想再挑起另一场争端。

sentences.en: And I think the Smithsonian board started to worry that this was exactly the kind of hot button issue that would set off the Trump administration.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们开始进行内部讨论，考虑是否将这幅画从展览中撤下。

sentences.en: And they were not spoiling for another fight.
sentences.zh: 当谢拉德风闻这个想法时，她很不高兴，并选择取消整个展览。

sentences.en: So they started to have internal discussions about perhaps pulling it from the show.
sentences.zh: 她基本上觉得博物馆触碰了某种红线，听起来就像是进入了审查的领域。

sentences.en: And when Sherald got wind of this idea, she was not happy about it and chose to cancel the entire thing.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全如此。

sentences.en: She basically felt like the museum had crossed some kind of red line and into it sounds like censorship, basically.
sentences.zh: 我认为这件事同样令人不安的是，这是史密森尼决定自我审查，甚至在特朗普政府提出任何抱怨之前就已经这样做了。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 既然政府甚至没有要求，那政府对她退展有什么反应吗？

sentences.en: And I think what was also troubling about this was this was the Smithsonian deciding to censor itself, even in advance of any complaints from the Trump administration.
sentences.zh: 政府对这一决定表示庆祝，甚至几乎试图将此归功于自己。

sentences.en: Did the administration react at all to her pulling out since they hadn't even asked for it?
sentences.zh: 一位白宫官员将这件作品描述为“试图通过分裂和意识形态的镜头来重新诠释我们国家最神圣的符号之一”。

sentences.en: The administration celebrated this decision and almost seemed to try to take credit for it.
sentences.zh: 所以这正是特朗普政府一直以来在寻求的那种努力或对某些艺术表达的压制。

sentences.en: A White House official described the work as an effort to reinterpret one of our nation's most sacred symbols through a divisive and ideological lens.
sentences.zh: 你知道，

sentences.en: So this was exactly the kind of effort or kind of curtailing of certain artistic expression that the Trump administration has been seeking.
sentences.zh: 听起来史密森尼确实陷入了两难境地，因为他们试图在不惹恼特朗普政府太多的同时保持一定水平的独立性。

sentences.en: You know,
sentences.zh: 然而他们却仍在做出所有这些让步。

sentences.en: it really sounds like the Smithsonian is really stuck between a rock and a hard place because they're trying to maintain some level of independence without angering the Trump administration too much.
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇，这些让步会进行到什么程度，才能真正安抚特朗普政府？

sentences.en: And yet they're still making all of these concessions.
sentences.zh: 一点也不。

sentences.en: And so I wonder how far are these concessions going and actually appeasing the Trump administration?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果有的话，压力反而升级了。

sentences.en: Not far at all.
sentences.zh: 8月12日，政府宣布了一项基本上相当于对展览进行审计的决定，包括目前正在进行的和计划中的展览。

sentences.en: I mean, if anything, the pressure ramps up.
sentences.zh: 它给史密森尼设定了120天的最后期限，以做出其希望看到的具体改变。

sentences.en: On August 12th, the administration announced what essentially amounted to an audit of exhibitions, both those currently underway and those planned for the future.
sentences.zh: 在那段时间里，史密森尼必须用政府认为可以接受的描述，替换白宫认为具有分裂性或受意识形态驱使的任何语言。

sentences.en: It gave the Smithsonian a deadline of 120 days to make concrete changes that it wanted to see.
sentences.zh: 因此，这对史密森尼的独立性和使命来说是一个非常崭新的挑战。

sentences.en: And in that time, the Smithsonian had to replace any language that the White House deemed divisive or driven by ideology with descriptions that the administration found acceptable.
sentences.zh: 所以这真的是对史密森尼独立性和使命的一个全新挑战。

sentences.en: So this is a very new challenge to the Smithsonian's independence and mission.
sentences.zh: 所以，这对史密森尼的独立与使命而言，无疑是一场全新的严峻挑战。

sentences.en: And it really begs the question of how is Lonnie Bunch and the Smithsonian Institution going to respond?
sentences.zh: 这就引发了一个问题：朗尼·邦奇和史密森尼学会将如何回应？

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Winnalou.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜露。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我是《连线》游戏的作者，这是《纽约时报》游戏中的谜题之一。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢试图捉弄你。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖斯基，我每天都制作拼写蜜蜂和字母盒游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉的东西。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 当我听音乐时我能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由真人制作的，就像你刚刚听到的人一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com/games 即可从今天开始游戏。

sentences.en: Robin, you said that the administration has really started raising some specific objections at the Smithsonian.
sentences.zh: 罗宾，你说过政府确实开始对史密森尼学会提出一些具体的反对意见。

sentences.en: So can you give us a few examples of the exhibits that they actually have taken issue with?
sentences.zh: 那么你能给我们举几个他们实际提出异议的展览的例子吗？

sentences.en: Well, they actually come back to the Smithsonian with a real list of some of the exhibitions and content that they find objectionable.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们实际上带着一份真正的展览和内容清单回到了史密森尼学会，他们认为这些内容令人反感。

sentences.en: In a document that's titled President Trump is Right About the Smithsonian, they highlight several examples.
sentences.zh: 在一份题为《特朗普总统对史密森尼学会的看法是正确的》的文件中，他们强调了几个例子。

sentences.en: Among them is an exhibition that features art commemorating the act of crossing the southern border.
sentences.zh: 其中包括一个以纪念越过南部边境的行为为主题的艺术展。

sentences.en: They call out an installation of the pride flag, a stop-motion drawing animation examining the career of Anthony Fauci.
sentences.zh: 他们点名了一个骄傲旗的装置艺术，以及一个审视安东尼·福奇职业生涯的定格动画。

sentences.en: But what they really focus on is the issue of slavery and feeling that the Smithsonian overemphasizes slavery.
sentences.zh: 但他们真正关注的是奴隶制问题，他们觉得史密森尼学会过分强调了奴隶制。

sentences.en: In its exhibitions, they cite, for example, an installation at the American History Museum on Benjamin Franklin that looks at his achievements around electricity,
sentences.zh: 在他们的展览中，他们举例说，美国历史博物馆里有一个关于本杰明·富兰克林的装置艺术，展示了他在电力方面的成就，

sentences.en: but also talks about the fact that the people who enabled those experiments were enslaved people in his household.
sentences.zh: 但也谈到了这样一个事实，即促成这些实验的人是他家中的被奴役者。

sentences.en: And this is reflected in the post that Trump put up recently where he said that he considered the Smithsonian out of control where everything discussed, quote,
sentences.zh: 这反映在特朗普最近发布的一篇帖文中，他说他认为史密森尼学会失控了，讨论的一切，引述如下，

sentences.en: is how horrible our country is, how bad slavery was.
sentences.zh: 都是关于我们的国家有多糟糕，奴隶制有多糟糕。

sentences.en: And a lot of what the Trump administration is essentially reacting to is a kind of wholesale racial reckoning that took place in the wake of the George Floyd murder and has been underway at institutions around the country since 2020.
sentences.zh: 特朗普政府本质上做出的大部分反应，是对乔治·弗洛伊德谋杀案发生后发生的一种全面的种族清算，这种清算自2020年以来一直在全国各地的机构中进行。

sentences.en: How did that reckoning play out specifically in the museum world and the art world?
sentences.zh: 这种清算具体如何在博物馆界和艺术界展开？

sentences.en: Well,
sentences.zh: 嗯，

sentences.en: I think that it was a real kind of moment of truth for these institutions where they started to take a hard look at themselves and whether or not they accurately reflected the sort of diversity and range in our country.
sentences.zh: 我认为对这些机构来说，这是一个真正的真理时刻，它们开始严厉审视自己，以及它们是否准确反映了我们国家的多元化和广度。

sentences.en: And that had to do with everything from what was on their walls, what they showed, to the kind of artwork they acquired,
sentences.zh: 这与一切都有关，从墙上的展品、展出的内容，到他们收购的艺术品，

sentences.en: to the leadership who sat in the boardrooms and the directors of these museuMs.
sentences.zh: 再到董事会里的领导层和这些博物馆的馆长。

sentences.en: The Baltimore Museum of Art, for example, pledged to acquire only work by female artists for a year.
sentences.zh: 例如，巴尔的摩艺术博物馆承诺在一年内只收购女性艺术家的作品。

sentences.en: The Met also acknowledged that it had neglected the Harlem Renaissance.
sentences.zh: 大都会艺术博物馆也承认它忽视了哈莱姆文艺复兴。

sentences.en: And there were many people, you know, in the art world and in the broader culture who felt that this was a revision that was overdue.
sentences.zh: 你知道，艺术界和更广泛的文化界有许多人认为这种修正早就该进行了。

sentences.en: But there was also a camp that felt that it amounted to an overcorrection, that perhaps it had gone too far.
sentences.zh: 但也有一个阵营认为，这相当于矫枉过正，或许有点走得太远了。

sentences.en: And that when you're dealing with someone like Ben Franklin,
sentences.zh: 当你在处理像本杰明·富兰克林这样的人物时，

sentences.en: shouldn't we perhaps be focusing on his scientific contributions and not so much his flaws or his history of owning slaves?
sentences.zh: 我们难道不应该把重点放在他的科学贡献上，而不是他身上的缺点或拥有奴隶的历史吗？

sentences.en: Obviously, though, figuring out how to portray a complicated history is not a new idea for museums and certainly not a new idea for the Smithsonian.
sentences.zh: 不过很明显，弄清楚如何描绘复杂的历史对博物馆来说并不是一个新想法，对史密森尼学会来说当然也不是新想法。

sentences.en: And I think a lot of people understand that the work of historians and curators is in part, maybe large part,
sentences.zh: 我想很多人都明白，历史学家和策展人的工作在很大程度上，

sentences.en: figuring out how to portray and revisit and reimagine perhaps ugly parts of our history.
sentences.zh: 是弄清楚如何描绘、重新审视并重新构想我们历史中或许丑陋的部分。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: This is definitely not the first time the Smithsonian has been at the center of a debate about how history is told.
sentences.zh: 这绝对不是史密森尼学会第一次成为关于如何讲述历史的辩论的中心。

sentences.en: One famous example is from the 1990s.
sentences.zh: 一个著名的例子来自20世纪90年代。

sentences.en: The Air and Space Museum planned an exhibition around the bomber plane called the Enola Gay, which dropped the first atomic bomb on Hiroshima.
sentences.zh: 航空航天博物馆计划围绕名为“埃诺拉·盖伊”的轰炸机举办一个展览，该轰炸机向广岛投下了第一颗原子弹。

sentences.en: And originally it included details about Japanese victims and it talked about it as a mixed moral legacy.
sentences.zh: 最初它包含了关于日本受害者的细节，并将其讨论为一种复杂的道德遗产。

sentences.en: And there was a real outcry from veterans groups and members of Congress who felt that the thrust of the exhibit had become too negative.
sentences.zh: 退伍军人团体和国会议员对此强烈抗议，他们认为展览的核心方向变得太负面了。

sentences.en: And in response to that,
sentences.zh: 作为回应，

sentences.en: there were actually adjustments made to kind of moderate the telling of that episode so that it didn't necessarily dwell on some of the uglier aspects of the bomb.
sentences.zh: 实际上做出了一些调整，以缓和对那一集历史的讲述，这样它就不一定会过分渲染炸弹更丑陋的一些方面。

sentences.en: So there is a long history of debating how history gets told, but this is an unusual instance of the presidential administration imposing its will on how that story gets told.
sentences.zh: 因此，关于如何讲述历史的辩论有着悠久的历史，但这确实是一个罕见的例子，即总统行政机构将自己的意志强加于这一历史讲述的方式。

sentences.en: Which brings us to what is happening right now with the Smithsonian and the pressure for the Smithsonian to change what it actually displays in its museums against what some people would say is its very mission,
sentences.zh: 这就把我们带到了史密森尼学会目前正在发生的事情，以及史密森尼学会面临的压力，即改变其博物馆实际展示的内容，这与一些人所说的其核心使命背道而驰，

sentences.en: which is to be independent.
sentences.zh: 也就是保持独立性。

sentences.en: So where do you think stand with the administration's demands?
sentences.zh: 那么你认为对于政府的要求现在立场如何？

sentences.en: Well, the response from the Smithsonian really lies with its governing board, which is called the Board of Regents.
sentences.zh: 嗯，史密森尼学会的回应实际上在于其管理委员会，被称为董事会。

sentences.en: It has 17 members that include members of Congress, both Democrats and Republicans, as well as civilians.
sentences.zh: 它有17名成员，包括民主党和共和党国会议员以及平民成员。

sentences.en: Interestingly, it also includes the vice president, J.D.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，它还包括副总统J·D·

sentences.en: Vance.
sentences.zh: 万斯。

sentences.en: And it is overseen and run by John Roberts, the chief justice of the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 它由最高法院首席大法官约翰·罗伯茨监督和领导。

sentences.en: And Chief Justice Roberts famously is an institutionalist who is looking to avoid controversy, to focus on procedure and rules and not to enter partisan debates.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，首席大法官罗伯茨是一位建制派人物，他希望避免争议，专注于程序和规则，而不卷入党派辩论。

sentences.en: So we're waiting.
sentences.zh: 所以我们在等待。

sentences.en: It's been several weeks.
sentences.zh: 已经过去好几个星期了。

sentences.en: We know Bunch had lunch with the president last week, but we don't know exactly what happened there except that the meeting was described as cordial.
sentences.zh: 我们知道邦奇上周和总统共进午餐，但我们不知道具体发生了什么，只知道这次会面被描述为亲切的。

sentences.en: But there is still no official response from the Smithsonian to the White House's list of demands.
sentences.zh: 但史密森尼学会对白宫的需求清单仍然没有官方回应。

sentences.en: And it's a big moment for Bunch and the Smithsonian.
sentences.zh: 对于邦奇和史密森尼学会来说，这是一个重大的时刻。

sentences.en: Will they take a stand and enforce the independence of the Smithsonian or not?
sentences.zh: 他们会表明立场并捍卫史密森尼学会的独立性吗？

sentences.en: What would it look like for Lonnie Bunch to take a stand?
sentences.zh: 如果朗尼·邦奇表明立场会是什么样子？

sentences.en: And what would it look like if that stand didn't work?
sentences.zh: 如果这种立场不起作用又会是什么样子？

sentences.en: Well, I think if Lonnie Bunch says this is our purview and not yours,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想如果朗尼·邦奇说这是我们的权限而不是你们的，

sentences.en: then the Trump administration is likely to not be satisfied with that because basically the Smithsonian would be refusing to abide by this mandate.
sentences.zh: 那么特朗普政府可能不会对此满意，因为基本上史密森尼学会将拒绝遵守这一授权。

sentences.en: Right now, Trump doesn't have the votes on the board to dominate decision making, but that could change in a short amount of time.
sentences.zh: 目前，特朗普在董事会中没有足够的票数来主导决策，但在短时间内情况可能会改变。

sentences.en: In a few months, several members are due to cycle off, and members do need to be approved by Congress,
sentences.zh: 几个月后，几名成员即将离任，而成员确实需要得到国会的批准，

sentences.en: and Trump could have a lot more influence in appointing those who succeed them, and then he would have control of the board going forward.
sentences.zh: 特朗普在任命他们的继任者时可能会有更多影响力，然后他将在未来控制董事会。

sentences.en: And that's largely what is expected to happen.
sentences.zh: 这在很大程度上也是各方所预期的结果。

sentences.en: This is really reminding me of this old adage about how history gets written by the victors, right, like by the people in charge.
sentences.zh: 这真的让我想起了一句老话，关于历史是由胜利者书写，就像由掌权者书写一样，对吧？

sentences.en: And Trump is the one in charge, and he's trying to, as you said, impose his version of history on the institutions that help define it for the broad American public.
sentences.zh: 特朗普是掌权者，正如你所说，他正试图将他的历史版本强加给那些帮助广大美国公众定义历史的机构。

sentences.en: We're obviously in a moment of backlash against what some people see as an overcorrection in 2020.
sentences.zh: 我们显然正处于对某些人认为2020年矫枉过正的现象进行强烈反弹的时刻。

sentences.en: And so I wonder, is what we're seeing now just another swing of the cultural pendulum that could, of course, swing back with a new administration?
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇，我们现在看到的只是文化钟摆的又一次摆动，当然它可能会随着新政府的到来而摆回去吗？

sentences.en: Or is what we're seeing more enduring?
sentences.zh: 还是我们看到的具有更持久的影响？

sentences.en: I do think that this is a moment where larger questions are on the table, and we're not sure of the answers.
sentences.zh: 我确实认为这是一个摆出更大问题的时刻，而我们并不确定答案。

sentences.en: And, you know, historically, art institutions and artists have been kind of the watchdogs of our nation to some extent,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，从历史上看，艺术机构和艺术家在某种程度上一直是国家的看门人，

sentences.en: and the victors in culture wars, that free expression has carried the day.
sentences.zh: 也是文化战争中的胜利者，言论自由取得了最终胜利。

sentences.en: And this is a case where you actually see an administration and a political point of view kind of shutting that down.
sentences.zh: 而在这种情况下，你实际上看到一个行政机构和一种政治观点在某种程度上扼杀这一点。

sentences.en: And I think there is some concern that that could have lasting, chilling effects.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们确实担心这可能会产生持久的寒蝉效应。

sentences.en: It's certainly one we're already seeing in institutions across the country, besides the Smithsonian, a sort of anticipation of needing to be silenced.
sentences.zh: 这当然是我们已经在除了史密森尼学会之外全国各地的机构中看到的一种情况，一种需要保持沉默的某种预期。

sentences.en: And I had lunch today with a European museum director who said that he saw this as a frightening pattern
sentences.zh: 我今天和一位欧洲博物馆馆长共进午餐，他说他认为这是一种可怕的模式，

sentences.en: in terms of having seen this happen in other countries under authoritarian regimes where propaganda infects almost everything.
sentences.zh: 因为他看到这种现象在其他国家威权政体下发生，宣传渗透到几乎所有事情中。

sentences.en: And there is worry about what this moment means for scholarly independence and artistic expression.
sentences.zh: 人们担心这个时刻对学术独立和艺术表达意味着什么。

sentences.en: A lot of museum leaders feel this is a moment to take a firm stand in favor of open debate and critical thinking and freedom of expression,
sentences.zh: 许多博物馆馆长认为，这是一个坚定立场以支持公开辩论、批判性思维和言论自由的时刻，

sentences.en: which are foundational values of American cultural institutions.
sentences.zh: 这些是美国文化机构的基本价值观。

sentences.en: At the same time, they also want to protect their organizations from landing in the crosshairs of the Trump administration right now,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，他们也希望保护自己的组织免于现在就落入特朗普政府的攻击目标，

sentences.en: which could threaten them in a more long-term way.
sentences.zh: 这可能会以更长远的方式威胁到他们。

sentences.en: And I think they're also seeing that outrage doesn't have a whole lot of effect.
sentences.zh: 我想他们也看到愤怒并没有起到太大的作用。

sentences.en: So the result is places just keeping their heads down.
sentences.zh: 因此结果就是各地只能低调行事。

sentences.en: Robin, if the president was, in fact, able to gain control of America's attic, as you put it earlier,
sentences.zh: 罗宾，如果正如你刚才所说，总统事实上能够控制美国的阁楼，

sentences.en: I wonder what you think that means just in terms of curating the story of America and presenting it to the public.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你认为这在策展美国的故事并将其呈现给公众方面意味着什么。

sentences.en: I think what it means is that he would have remade these institutions in his own image as kind of an extenuation of his values, his worldview, and his priorities.
sentences.zh: 我认为这意味着他将按照自己的形象重塑这些机构，作为他的价值观、世界观和优先事项的延伸。

sentences.en: I think it will also be a simplified version of America, a story with kind of less nuance and complexity.
sentences.zh: 我认为这也将是美国的一个简化版本，一个带有更少细微差别和复杂性的故事。

sentences.en: And interestingly, in Lonnie Bunch's memoir, he recalls during the first Trump administration walking the president
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，在朗尼·邦奇的回忆录中，他回忆起在第一届特朗普政府期间，陪同总统

sentences.en: through the National Museum of African-American History and Culture when it had just opened and that the president didn't want to see anything too difficult.
sentences.zh: 参观刚刚开馆的国家非裔美国人历史文化博物馆时，总统不想看任何太困难的东西。

sentences.en: And Bunch writes that actually it's really important to look at history's fullness and complexity, even though that can be hard to do.
sentences.zh: 邦奇写道，事实上，审视历史的完整性和复杂性非常重要，尽管这做起来可能很艰难。

sentences.en: All of this is coming to a head as the president has talked a lot about the upcoming 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence next summer.
sentences.zh: 所有这一切都在迎来高潮，因为总统最近谈了很多关于明年夏天即将迎来的《独立宣言》签署250周年纪念日。

sentences.en: I think the president has made clear he would like that to be largely celebratory.
sentences.zh: 我认为总统已经明确表示，他希望这在很大程度上是庆祝性的。

sentences.en: And it really raises questions about what kind of a country we're going to be commemorating on an anniversary like that.
sentences.zh: 这确实引发了人们对我们将在这样的周年纪念日上纪念一个什么样的国家的疑问。

sentences.en: Is it one where we are just sort of applauding progress as triumphant?
sentences.zh: 这是一个我们只是把进步当作胜利来欢呼的国家吗？

sentences.en: Or are we looking more frankly and squarely at progress in all its complexity as being both our successes and our failures?
sentences.zh: 还是我们在更坦率、更直接地看待包含所有复杂性的进步，认为它既有成功也有失败？

sentences.en: That mix is also very much a part of who we are and what there is to celebrate.
sentences.zh: 这种混合也是我们是谁以及有什么值得庆祝的重要部分。

sentences.en: Robin, thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 罗宾，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你邀请我。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他内容。

sentences.en: Google avoided the harshest penalties in a landmark antitrust case when a federal judge ruled on Tuesday that while Google needed to hand over some of its search data to rivals,
sentences.zh: 周二，一名联邦法官裁定，虽然谷歌需要将其部分搜索数据移交给竞争对手，但谷歌在一次具有里程碑意义的反垄断诉讼中避免了最严厉的惩罚，

sentences.en: it did not have to give in to the government's toughest demands, including spinning off its Chrome browser.
sentences.zh: 它不必屈服于政府最严厉的要求，包括剥离其谷歌浏览器业务。

sentences.en: The ruling is a blow to the government's push in recent years to challenge the dominance of the biggest tech companies, including Google, Apple, Amazon, and Meta,
sentences.zh: 这一裁决对政府近年来的行动是一个打击，政府一直试图挑战包括谷歌、苹果、亚马逊和元宇宙在内的最大科技公司的统治地位，

sentences.en: which both the Biden and Trump administrations have accused of anti-competitive behavior.
sentences.zh: 拜登和特朗普两届政府都指责这些公司存在反竞争行为。

sentences.en: And in a stunning departure from the traditional tactics of America's war on drugs,
sentences.zh: 在一项惊人地偏离美国禁毒战争传统策略的举动中，

sentences.en: President Trump said on Tuesday that the military had carried out a strike against a boat run by a Venezuelan, quote, narco-terrorist organization.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统周二表示，军方对一艘由委内瑞拉所谓的“毒品恐怖主义组织”运营的船只进行了打击。

sentences.en: The move comes as the Trump administration has stepped up its belligerent rhetoric about fighting drug cartels
sentences.zh: 在此之前，特朗普政府升级了其关于打击贩毒集团的好战言论，

sentences.en: and has labeled Venezuela's president, Nicolás Maduro, as a terrorist cartel leader.
sentences.zh: 并将委内瑞拉总统尼古拉斯·马杜罗标为恐怖分子贩毒集团头目。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Sydney Harper, Olivia Natt, and Claire Tennisgetter.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由悉尼·哈珀、奥利维亚·纳特和克莱尔·特尼斯盖特制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Patricia Willans and was engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 由帕特里夏·威兰斯编辑，克里斯·伍德担任音频工程。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Rachel AbraMs.
sentences.zh: 我是雷切尔·阿布拉姆斯。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《连线秀》中，我们正在为假期招待客人做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人宾至如归的秘诀。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是需要完全黑暗才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是不是喝断片去睡觉。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们需要什么样的光线？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的要求。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有对什么过敏或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢喝咖啡还是茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》应用程序或你喜欢收听的任何地方查找《连线秀》。
